email.body1:
Dave, saw Forethought is being acquired by Zendesk, their biggest deal in nearly 20 years, right after crossing $1B in customer ROI.

An acquisition like that opens far more enterprise accounts worth reaching than reps can personally cover, and good ones go quiet while the team works the obvious logos. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Forethought off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Dave, quick follow-up for Forethought.

Post-acquisition, the addressable base expands fast and named accounts per rep climb, yet most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the number. The gap shows up late, then the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings the team needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Dave, last bit of proof for Forethought.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Forethought's reply rate likely compares to peer enterprise-AI teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Dave, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise coverage without adding reps is not a priority right now, no problem at all. An acquisition is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise-AI motion? I will tailor it either way.
